title: Unified 6-Level UI Surface System
description: Replace the dual Level (base|canvas|window|panel|overlay|temporary) + GlassTier (panel|ribbon|menu|windowOptions) systems with a single formula-derived 6-level system: base -> window -> pane -> panel -> dialog -> menu. Each level's background darkens (light mode) / lightens (dark mode) and its glass (blur+alpha) increases, derived from base knobs via oklab color-mix, not hand-tuned. No element manually assigns fill/glass -- everything inherits from data-level CSS cascade. Applies across ui/js/react, ui/styling, the OS shell (framework/renderer/react), coda desktop/assistant, cad/renderer, infinite, animate, legacy compose apps, Storybook, and the native wgpu mirror (ui/wgpu/rs, framework/renderer/wgpu/rs). Full design in /Users/ueli/.claude/plans/all-ui-elements-are-fizzy-shore.md.
summary: Follow-up to the 6-level UI surface rollout: enforced "one level = one appearance" structurally instead of by convention. Root causes fixed: (D1) cn()'s tailwind-merge instance had no class group for ui-surface/ui-glass/ui-veil, so composing a fill after bg-transparent silently kept both classes and CSS declaration-order (not intent) picked the winner -- extended the bg-color group so these three fills mutually conflict with every bg-* utility, last-in-cn deterministically wins; found and fixed the one call site whose order this flipped (mode-dock drag-preview cap). (D2) windowChromeTitleChipClass baked in an opaque surfaceClass on interior chips (introduction title, step counter, context-menu title) sitting inside an already-painted chip-cap cell -- removed it. (D3) ui-surface was composed alongside bg-active-base and always won, silently killing the active mode-dock tab highlight -- removed the redundant fill so the highlight renders. (D4) swept and fixed ~15 other interior-paint drift sites (opaque mode-dock tabs on glass tabbars, double glass in the measures rail, opaque Command/TabsList inside already-glass hosts, a level-fill used as a selection highlight, Navbar/Footer/TutorialBar painting with no data-level stamp, a nested ui-surface in framework/renderer/react, coda's glass title bar over an opaque window root). (D5) added the actual enforcement API: SurfaceFill/surfaceFillClass, SurfaceScope (LevelProvider + a new SurfaceContext), useSurface(), and a Surface component that stamps data-level, paints exactly one fill, and dev-warns when nested inside an ancestor already painting the same level -- wired into WindowChrome and all Radix portal content (Popover/Tooltip/HoverCard/Select/Dialog/breadcrumb-dropdown/UIDialog/tutorial captions). Deleted the now-redundant glassChromeClass alias after migrating its ~15 consumers across ui/js/react and framework/renderer/react. Added a direct regression test reproducing the reported bug (introduction step's title chip, close cell, body, and footer chips must all render the identical dialog-level glass) plus cn-semantics, useSurface, and Surface dev-warning tests, extending the existing inline vitest block only. Verified: ui-react full suite stable at the same ~9 pre-existing/unrelated failures (icon-catalog rework, three.js gumball mock, tree-guide tests, driver-config) with zero new failures; framework-renderer-react test-quick unchanged (3 pre-existing icon-name failures); cargo check on ui_wgpu clean; coda-desktop build blocked only by the already-flagged, separately-tracked stale Storybook fixture issue (task_d0e966e6), unrelated to this change. Full verification log in the ticket folder.
